properties.description: scripts/run_bulk_extraction.py --dry-run calls spend.declare() BEFORE branching on the dry-run flag, so a dry run writes a ceiling declaration onto the append-only spend ledger (state/spend_ledger.jsonl) for a run that never dispatches a call. A dry run exists to PRICE a run before committing to it; declaring is the commitment. Consequences: (a) a caller who only wants a projection must invent a --ceiling-tokens value, and that fabricated number is then permanently on the ledger as a declared ceiling with the task file named as its authority; (b) the real ceiling, derived from the dry run's own output, must then be a superseding re-declare, so the ledger reads as an operator ceiling correction when nothing was corrected. Found while executing chunked_pilot ADDENDUM-03 §2 on 2026-08-29: the section specified this runner, and scripts/chunked_pilot.py --phase dry_run was used instead and the discrepancy reported in the RESULT. Fix: move the declare() call inside the non-dry-run branch and make --ceiling-tokens not required when --dry-run is set. Second, smaller defect in the same command: --dry-run has no chunker, so under a chunked profile it prints whole documents and cannot produce the per-document chunk counts a chunked profile needs priced.

properties.description: Design the standing dispatcher (L4 gap: dispatch latency, not decision-making). Evidence from 2026-08-31/09-01: auto-registered gap tasks, ADDENDUM-03 with gate open, and zero-spend housekeeping all sat in `proposed` until a human relayed a dispatch line — the system solves problems into proposed state and then waits for a message bus. Build: a runner that polls Seldon for dispatchable tasks against HARD machine-checkable criteria only (declared ceiling within standing band; no liveness conflict on owned files/queues per a file-ownership model; gate conditions machine-verifiable; zero-spend tasks always eligible), launches CC headless per DD-019, and logs each dispatch decision as an event with the criteria evaluation. Operator touchpoints unchanged (spend above band, external sends, value inputs, incidents) — the dispatcher enforces the closed list instead of the operator enacting it. Design session first (Desktop): gate-condition language, file-ownership/lease model (two runners on one queue is the batch-identity class at runner grain — four instances say design this carefully), launchd scheduling, kill switch. Prior art: cron/CI schedulers, Wintermute's launchd morning-brief pipeline, the burn's own STOP-file convention, the wintermute lease/reaper mechanism.

Essay/paper: "Statistical boundaries can't be reasoned across; judgment boundaries can" — the decision-theoretic and philosophical grounding of this system's design, written for a general technical audience (distinct from f1da94c6, the FCSM methods paper). Spine: (1) small-world vs large-world decisions — Knight 1921 (risk vs uncertainty), Savage 1954 (small worlds), Wald 1945 (SPRT; statistical decisions spend judgment early, in the loss function), Meehl 1954 / Grove & Meehl 1996 (mechanical vs clinical prediction), Kahneman/Sibony/Sunstein 2021 Noise (bias vs noise; rules beat judges where rules can be written), Taleb (ludic fallacy, Black Swan). (2) The three boundaries: statistical (more data dissolves it; escalating intelligence adds nothing), judgment (model underdetermined; collapses to rules wherever weights can be stated — automation of judgment = converting one-off calls to standing policy, as this project's addenda did), accountability (non-epistemic; culpability needs a legal person; Elish "moral crumple zone"; per-decision sign-off at machine scale = liability sponge; the defensible form is ex-ante policy signature — sign the loss function/gates/ceilings, not each output — mirroring how statistical agencies sign methodology, not estimates). (3) Live exhibit: OpenAI/Hugging Face incident (July 2026, reports 2026-08-26 from OpenAI and METR/Redwood): reward hacking as Goodhart on the loss function; 93% of message-board discussion traced to 198 never-solved tasks — impossible evals with no safe exit redirect optimization at the scorer; contrast with this system's GATE UNREACHABLE refuse-not-verdict rule (DD-026, G1 fix) and pre-registered satisfiable gates. (4) Stigmergy (Grassé 1959, ant/bee coordination through environment traces): the unsanctioned message board as emergent stigmergy; event-sourced graph + task files as sanctioned stigmergy with provenance and admission gates; machine intelligence as its own kind (not deficient human intelligence) — design for what coordinates machines well, not what mimics humans. Sources: metr.org/blog/2026-08-26-openai-hugging-face-incident-investigation/, OpenAI 2026-08-26 report, thehackernews.com 2026-08 coverage. Register under ai-readiness-kg for now; venue TBD (blog/preprint). Desktop authors the CC task spec when prioritized.

Chunker overlap join costs recall on assembled documents. chunker.Chunk.grounding_text() returns overlap_text + '\n\n' + text; each part is a verbatim document substring but the CONCATENATION is not, so it only reproduces the document when the real split point was a blank line. A model span straddling that junction is chunk-valid and document-invalid, and phase_ingest's document-level re-validation rejects it (node_not_in_document / edge_not_in_document). Measured 2026-09-01 on chunk grounding_text NOT being a document substring: odcs 25/45, slsa 17/32 (both assembled by scripts/extent_remediation.py with '---' + heading + 'Source:' separators at section boundaries) vs fcsm-20-04 2/47 and w3c-dcat-3 0/42 (native documents). Cost on bulk_v038_b014: 18 nodes + 21 edges rejected, ~5 percent of proposals. This costs RECALL, not correctness -- nothing ungrounded entered the graph, and the re-validation is the guard working as designed. Two candidate fixes, neither safe mid-burn because changing chunk boundaries invalidates chunk-level resume for every batch: (a) have grounding_text() return the true document slice spanning overlap start to body end rather than a synthetic join; (b) have the extent-remediation assembler use blank-line-only separators. Prefer (a); it fixes the general case rather than one producer. Source: cc_tasks/2026-08-30_bulk_extraction_v038_RESULT.md ADDENDUM-03 section.

G1 EVAL v3 backlog (not queued; instrument frozen at v2 for the January pilot). Items, each with its motivating record in the v2 RESULT: (1) 25 holdout-motivated parser misses (dash ranges, "plausible range runs from", "at one standard error", two-year periods, "flagging for expert review", "could reasonably fall between"; §6.1 and §6.4). (2) Suppressed-cell propositions: schema extension `estimate: null` + SUPPRESSION qualifier; failure class `fabricated_estimate` = any numeric value bound to the suppressed row (§9.7). (3) H5 needs surfaces with varied footnote distance (all v2 distances ~13k chars). (4) Freeze procedure: freeze commit is the last act of the step, after the prior-evidence re-score passes (§9.1). (5) C1 wording vs code disagreement on reversals inside overlapping intervals — pre-register one rule. (6) Vintage on release surfaces: month-without-year loss class. Prerequisite for any v3 run: reviewer calibration (κ) from the 2026-09-03 blind sample task.

properties.name: g1 freeze calibration redefinition findings
g1_calibration_sheet_2026-09-03
properties.description: Blind reviewer-calibration sheet for G1 EVAL v2: a stratified random sample of 60 family records (seed 20260903, floor 3 per non-empty stratum, strata = scorer level x reviewer verdict) drawn from g1_v2_pooled_opus_reviewed.json (650) and g1_v2_control_reviewed.json (128). Carries only the prompt the consumer saw, the response verbatim, the estimate, the qualifier family and its published forms, the mode and the compression level - no scorer level, no reviewer verdict, no failure class, no surface type, no model id. CSV twin: assessment/results/g1_calibration_sheet_2026-09-03.csv. Task cc_tasks/2026-09-03_g1_freeze_calibration_redefinition_findings.md step 1.

properties.name: g1_calibration_key_2026-09-03
properties.description: PATH ONLY, deliberately not committed (gitignored by assessment/.gitignore results/* and by an explicit rule in .gitignore). The sample id -> record mapping for the blind calibration sheet: scorer level, reviewer verdict, target proposition, family, mode, compression, evidence path, plus the seed and the stratum table. Joining the sheet to the verdicts before the operator has labelled it would destroy the blinding the sheet exists for. Task cc_tasks/2026-09-03_g1_freeze_calibration_redefinition_findings.md step 1.

properties.name: g1_calibration_sample
properties.description: Draws the blind reviewer-calibration sample: stratified by scorer level x reviewer verdict, proportional allocation with a floor of 3 per non-empty stratum (largest remainder on the residual, capped at stratum size), fixed seed printed in the sheet. Writes the .md and .csv sheets and the gitignored key. Zero model calls. Tests: tests/test_g1_calibration_sample.py.

properties.name: g1_calibration_agreement
properties.description: Computes operator-vs-scorer agreement (Cohen's quadratic-weighted kappa on L0-L4, plus an unweighted six-category kappa including unparseable/U) and operator-vs-reviewer agreement on the review queue (binary genuine/parser_miss from a pre-registered implied-verdict rule), each with a percentile bootstrap 95% interval, raw agreement, a confusion table and positive specific agreement on parser_miss. No kappa threshold and no verbal band. Not run on real labels in the issuing task. Tests: tests/test_g1_calibration_agreement.py.

properties.name: g1_resolve_results
properties.description: Resolves {{result:NAME:field}} tokens against registered Seldon Results by replaying seldon_events.jsonl and matching properties.units (G1 Results carry their name there; seldon result register has no --name and this repo has no paper/ project, so seldon paper build cannot resolve them). Ambiguous names are fatal, never guessed. Zero model calls.

Operator labels the G1 reviewer-calibration sheet (assessment/results/g1_calibration_sheet_2026-09-03.md or .csv: 60 blind records, level L0-L4 or U plus a note per record), then run scripts/g1_calibration_agreement.py --sheet <filled> --key assessment/results/.g1_calibration_key_2026-09-03.json --out assessment/results/g1_calibration_agreement_<date>.json and register the kappas as Results. Until then the v2 genuine-loss counts rest on an unmeasured LLM reviewer. Issued by cc_tasks/2026-09-03_g1_freeze_calibration_redefinition_findings.md step 1.

properties.name: dd-037-g1-independent-rater-calibration
properties.title: DD-037: G1's reviewer is calibrated against an independent model; the consequence is a reported range, not a verdict
properties.description: Design decision DD-037 (2026-09-03): the second rater for the G1 calibration is an independent model (claude-fable-5-1, with the reviewer's own model refused by name), not the operator; independence is enforced by a different model family, a hermetic cwd, one record per call and a prompt carrying only the blind sheet's instructions and one record. The consequence rule is a RANGE — the reviewer's genuine-loss count is never reported alone, but between the scorer's count and the rater-implied count, with kappa stating the width; no threshold, no Landis & Koch band. The operator's only touchpoint is an optional disagreement list, and the G1 touchpoint list is closed. States plainly that the coefficient measures agreement between two instruments and not the correctness of either, and records a limit of the pre-registered implied-verdict rule on unparseable records without patching it. Amends DD-036 item 3. Task cc_tasks/2026-09-03_g1_calibration_rating_agreement.md step 4.

properties.name: dd-038-g1-binary-score-levels-descriptive
properties.title: DD-038: G1-O is scored on the binary L3+ share; the level scale beneath it is descriptive
properties.description: Design decision DD-038 (2026-09-03): the calibration found the instrument robust at the L3+/below-L3 grain (18 of 18 preserved-exact records, 14 of 14 reviewer parser-misses, genuine-loss range 173-178 of 232) and not at the level grain (exact-level agreement 0 of 5 in the L2 stratum and 0 of 4 in L0; quadratic-weighted kappa 0.392 [0.205, 0.614] against 0.421 [0.206, 0.665] on the binary verdict). G1-O's score has always been the binary; the five levels stay descriptive. The level-based pre-registered statements E5 and E6 keep their coded verdicts, unchanged and unwithdrawn, each printed with the level agreement and labelled as the scorer's reading; E4/H3/H4/H5/C1 are L3+ claims and untouched. Any future level-based claim needs a level-agreement estimate at its own grain first. No kappa threshold is set. Builds on DD-033 (the scale) and DD-037 (the rater); nothing re-scored. Task cc_tasks/2026-09-03_g1_memo_v1_2_level_caveat.md step 3.

dd-039-result-tokens-resolve-by-name
properties.title: DD-039: Result tokens resolve by name against the graph; the SI-09 units fallback is no longer needed here
properties.description: Design decision DD-039 (2026-09-04): all 3,592 Results carry a name and every {{result:}} token resolves by name against the graph, not by matching the token key against a units property. 953 names keep their uppercase level and qualifier-class segments under AD-028's amended grammar; no Result was renamed to satisfy a lint. 63 rows the migration declines to name automatically were named slug(units)__<artifact_id[:8]> deterministically, none being cited by any token; the 23 real-unit rows keep their units. Operational consequence: SI-09 transitional fallback resolutions went from 73 across three documents (66 memo, 4 design_decisions, 3 deck draft) to ZERO, so the fallback can be removed upstream with no effect here and any future SI-09 line for this project is a regression. properties.name: dd-040-kg-figures-must-resolve-to-results
properties.title: DD-040: KG figures quoted anywhere must resolve to a kg_diag_* or cq_v1_* Result
properties.description: Design decision DD-040 (2026-09-04): diagnostic-in-chat is the defect; scripts/kg_diagnostic.py plus a dated snapshot DataFile and 52 kg_diag_* Results is the mechanism that replaces it. Re-derivation confirmed 19 of 20 quoted figures exactly - the chat numbers were right but unverified - while the twentieth was wrong in a material way: 72 of 211 Documents have no extraction edges, so a third of the corpus is admitted and unextracted. Three further first-run differences were bugs in the new script (Cypher aggregates grouped by n.name and by nothing, which merges duplicate-named nodes), recorded in the script where they happened. Rule: any graph figure in a handoff, memo, decision or task file must resolve by name to a kg_diag_* or cq_v1_* Result. Task cc_tasks/2026-09-04_kg_diagnostic_and_cq_harness.md section 0.2.

Effect: a provenance-traceback question answered through the ASSERTS edge silently omits them. The doc_id property means the loss is recoverable; whether the extraction emitted no asserts edge or the projection dropped it is NOT determined here. properties.description: SECOND FINDING of task section 2, answered rather than left open: Concept.key is DOCUMENT-SCOPED BY DESIGN and is not a canonical identifier. Evidence: format is <doc_id>::<item_id> (scripts/build_projection.py:335 node_key); 8,662 Concepts carry 8,662 DISTINCT keys, i.e. one per node; and ZERO keys are shared across more than one doc_id. The design comment at build_projection.py:328-332 states the intent and the reason - '600 of 6,988 item ids recur across documents; keying nodes by bare item id FUSED them. Every non-Document node is keyed by the composite (document_id, item_id)... Cross-document identity is dedup's job, never the loader's' (DD-020). So the 1,122 duplicate-name Concept groups covering 3,479 nodes are not a loader defect: they are the loader behaving as specified, with the dedup pass that was meant to follow never having been run. Consequence for the CQ measurement: no property in the graph can be used as a canonical key, which is why the collapse in assessment/cq/collapse.py has to canonicalise the display text at query time. NOT A DEFECT AND NOT FIXED - registered so the next reader does not mistake key for an identity they can join on.

STRUCTURAL: admission does not enqueue extraction, so never_queued is the pipeline's normal state after a document is admitted. Evidence: 233 documents carry a manifest_add event; only 68 have ever had an extraction_request; 165 admitted documents have never been requested. CODE LOCATION: kg/manifest.py emits manifest_add and nothing else - grep for 'extraction_request' in kg/manifest.py and kg/eventlog.py returns nothing. A request is emitted only by an explicit later action: kg/queue_cli.py:174 ('emitted N extraction_request events') or scripts/run_bulk_extraction.py:369 (the --docs override). The gate is deliberate and defensible - kg/queue.py:132 enforces preconditions at emit, and DD-024 makes semantic-edge extraction demand-pull rather than automatic - but the CONSEQUENCE is that a document can be admitted, hashed, projected as a Document node and cited in a memo while contributing nothing to the graph, with no event anywhere recording that a decision was taken. That is what 17 of the 72 unextracted documents are (the whole g1eval-2026-09-02 epoch): not deferred with a reason, simply never asked for. The 55 deferred documents are the contrasting case - they carry an extraction_deferred event with reason 'no consumer', so the decision is on the record and revivable. REGISTERED AS A FINDING, NOT FIXED, per task section 4. Measured by scripts/extraction_gap_diagnostic.py (Results kg_diag_gap_never_queued, kg_diag_gap_excluded_by_design).

properties.description: SPEND DEFECT: the systemic-failure guard in chunked_pilot.phase_extract stops the driver but not the spend already committed to the thread pool. Measured on run g1eval_extraction_2026-09-04 (2026-09-04/05): of 609 settles, 323 were success and 286 were error_with_output, the latter billing 15,073,098 tokens at the estimate for calls that produced no usable output — 49 percent of the 30.5M settled at that point. CAUSE: phase_extract submits EVERY future to the ThreadPoolExecutor up front ('futs = {pool.submit(...) for ...}'), then iterates results; when the streak reaches STOP_AFTER_FAILURES=5 it calls f.cancel() on the remainder, which only stops futures that have not started. Futures already dispatched to the 8 workers run to completion, each reserving and settling at the call-class estimate. The same loop then 'continue's past them without calling .result(), which is why the log printed 5 FAILED lines for 286 failures - the failures were real but never surfaced. TRIGGER: a Claude session/usage limit reaching the  subprocesses, which returns exit 1 with empty output (the same shape DD-022's empty_failure back-off was written for, but classified here as error_with_output because the CLI printed to stderr). SUGGESTED FIX (not applied - the run was live and the module is imported by the running process): submit in bounded waves of max_workers, or check the streak before each submit rather than only before each result, so a systemic failure cannot bill the whole remaining queue. REGISTERED AS A FINDING, NOT FIXED. Task cc_tasks/2026-09-04_extract_g1eval_17_and_rerun.md.

properties.name: run_g1eval_extraction
properties.description: Chunk-level extraction driver for the 17 g1eval-2026-09-02 prior-art sources: builds the cohort from the dixie epoch declaration intersected with the queue's record of an extraction_request, declares the run's ceiling on the shared DD-022 ledger, and delegates every extraction primitive to chunked_pilot (imported, not copied) under the pinned production profile bulk_v038.

properties.name: harvest_ai_ready_contexts
properties.description: Finds and locates every sentence in the unextracted corpus containing 'AI ready', 'AI-ready' or 'AI readiness', then merges a per-sentence sense classification (adoption / training_data / data_product_consumption / other) made by reading. Zero model spend (ADDENDUM-02 §3a).

properties.name: register_gap_results
properties.description: Registers the extraction-gap classification's figures as named Results, with a DD-041 rerun suffix. Exists because the first run registered its 16 kg_diag_gap_* Results from an ad-hoc command with no reproducible path.

properties.name: spend_ledger_2026-09-04_g1eval
properties.description: The shared DD-022 spend ledger as it stood after the g1eval extraction run: 974 settles under run_id g1eval_extraction_2026-09-04 (688 success, 286 error_with_output), the 13,280,000 declaration and the operator-authorized 69,000,000 supersede.

properties.name: g1eval_extraction_tokens_declared
properties.description: Tokens declared as the per-run ceiling for the g1eval extraction by the task file, priced at 664 chunks x the 20,000-token extraction_chunk FLOOR. The floor is the DD-022 guard's first-call reservation estimate, not a measurement, and DD-042 now forbids pricing a run from it. Superseded in flight to 69,000,000 on operator authorization (ADDENDUM-01 §1).

properties.name: g1eval_extraction_tokens_productive
properties.description: Tokens settled on the 688 calls that returned usable output (outcome_class=success) — the whole cohort, one settle per chunk. 45,494 tokens per chunk measured, 2.3x the call-class floor the ceiling was priced from (ADDENDUM-01 §1).

properties.name: g1eval_extraction_tokens_wasted
properties.description: Tokens settled on 286 calls whose output was discarded (outcome_class=error_with_output), 32.5% of the run. Cause: chunked_pilot.phase_extract submits every future up front and cancel() cannot stop a started one, so the systemic-failure guard stopped the driver while dispatched calls kept billing (Issue 830330b4, ADDENDUM-01 §2).

properties.name: cq_02_unextracted_sense_adoption
properties.description: Sentences in the 23 unextracted CQ-02 documents where 'AI ready/readiness' means an organization, sector or nation being ready to ADOPT AI (7 documents). Classified by reading; the classification is a judgement, the count is not (ADDENDUM-02 §3a).

properties.name: cq_02_unextracted_sense_training_data
properties.description: Sentences where the phrase means data prepared as INPUT to model training — cleaning, labelling, feature engineering, ML optimisation (11 documents). Classified by reading (ADDENDUM-02 §3a).

properties.name: cq_02_unextracted_sense_data_product_consumption
properties.description: Sentences where the phrase means a published data product's fitness to be discovered and correctly processed by an AI system at inference time — THE FRAMEWORK'S SENSE (13 documents). Classified by reading (ADDENDUM-02 §3a).

properties.name: cq_02_unextracted_sense_other
properties.description: Sentences carrying the phrase in running headers, contents listings, bibliographies, navigation markup, or generic statements whose sense cannot be determined from the sentence. Each carries a one-line reason in the JSONL (ADDENDUM-02 §3a).

properties.name: cq_02_unextracted_sentences_total
properties.description: Sentences containing 'AI ready', 'AI-ready' or 'AI readiness' across the 23 unextracted documents CQ-02's terms matched. Counted, not judged.

Sentences where the phrase means a published data product's fitness to be discovered and correctly processed by an AI system at inference time — THE FRAMEWORK'S SENSE. 68 sentences across 15 of the 23 documents. Classified by reading; the classification is a judgement, the count is not (ADDENDUM-02 §3a). Corrects this Result's first description, which said 13 documents.

properties.name: extract ai ready strand 11
run_strand_extraction

properties.name: strand_extraction_tokens_declared
properties.description: Per-run spend ceiling declared on state/spend_ledger.jsonl for run_id strand_extraction_2026-09-05, computed per DD-042 from the MEASURED rate rather than the call-class floor: 225 chunks x 45,493.38 tokens/chunk x 1.15 headroom. The rate is g1eval_extraction_tokens_productive (31,299,448) over the 688 chunks of the g1eval run. The floor-priced figure for the same work is 4,500,000, which is 2.6x too low — the same underestimate DD-042 exists to prevent. Task cc_tasks/2026-09-05_extract_ai_ready_strand_11.md §1.

WITHDRAWN GRAPH SUPPORT FOR THE G1 GAP CLAIM. The RESULT of 2026-09-04_kg_diagnostic_and_cq_harness quoted CQ-09's EMPTY answer (which Instruments MEASURES an uncertainty-related Concept) as the graph independently supporting the claim that G1 — uncertainty legibility in published data products — is the sharpest gap in the literature. RESULT-02 of 2026-09-04_extract_g1eval_17_and_rerun withdrew that support by measurement: after the g1eval extraction CQ-09 returns 10 raw / 5 collapsed rows (cq_v1_CQ_09_rows_raw_2026-09-04b = 10, cq_v1_CQ_09_rows_raw = 0). The instruments are Comunikos (mazzi-2021, owner Eurostat: 'designed to evaluate alternative ways of measuring and communicating data uncertainty specifically in contexts relevant to official economic statistics') and GRADE (van-der-bles-2019: 'a system designed to communicate indirect uncertainty'). The consequence runs through CQ-08, whose zero-instrument construct list fell from ten terms to six; 'uncertainty' is off it. THE CLAIM IS NOT FALSIFIED, IT IS UNSUPPORTED AS STATED. It survives only re-scoped to: no AI-READINESS ASSESSMENT INSTRUMENT measures uncertainty legibility. Comunikos and GRADE are uncertainty-communication research instruments, not readiness assessments, so the re-scoped claim is untested by CQ v1 — no v1 question joins an Instrument to the kind of framework that owns it. THE V2 COMPETENCY QUESTION THAT WOULD TEST IT: return every Instrument that (a) MEASURES a Concept whose surface form matches the uncertainty term set CQ-08 already uses, AND (b) whose parent Framework qualifies as an AI-readiness assessment — either by normative_status in the readiness/maturity family, or by carrying an ABOUT edge to a Concept in the AI-readiness cluster. An empty answer to THAT question is the evidence the memo's claim needs; an empty answer to CQ-09 was not. DO NOT EDIT THE MEMO OR THE DECK ON THIS ISSUE: if CQ set v2 answers the re-scoped question, that is an erratum then, on evidence. Registered by task cc_tasks/2026-09-05_extract_ai_ready_strand_11.md §4.

properties.name: strand_extraction_tokens_wasted

properties.name: strand_extraction_tokens_unsettled
properties.description: RESERVED (not measured) tokens on the two calls killed mid-flight when the run was restarted from 2 workers to 6 for throughput: bandi-2025-metadata-ai-ready#c0005 and #c0006, 43,810 each. Their subprocesses had run about a minute when the pass was stopped, so partial output was produced and discarded; both chunks were re-extracted cleanly in the second pass and both settled there. This is an ESTIMATE, stated as one because a killed call never settles and the guard's reservation is the only number that exists for it. It is the honest upper bound on the cost of the restart. Task cc_tasks/2026-09-05_extract_ai_ready_strand_11.md §2.

properties.resolution_notes: CLOSED BY RULE, task cc_tasks/2026-09-05_extract_ai_ready_strand_11.md §0.2 / DD-043 §3. Both halves are answered. (1) The 22 documents now HAVE Document nodes: kg_diag_gap_manifest_documents_without_a_document_node_2026-09-05 = 0, against 22 when this issue was filed. They were missing because they postdated the last projection replay; the replay in 2026-09-04_extract_g1eval_17_and_rerun created them. (2) The real question the issue left open - 'whether these 22 SHOULD become Document nodes is a real question and not answered here' - is now answered: they stay as Document nodes because that is what the G1 evaluation scores against, and they are never queued for extraction because nothing in them is a construct claim to be read. The mechanism is a rule, not 22 events: fixture_epochs: in dixie_evidence.yaml names g1dp-2026-09-02 / g1srp-2026-09-03 / g1sfc-2026-09-03, kg.queue.fixture_epochs() reads it, kg.queue.deferrals() overlays a synthetic eval_fixture deferral, and kg.queue.request() REFUSES a fixture document by name. The gap diagnostic therefore classifies them excluded_by_design, which drove kg_diag_gap_never_queued to 0 (from 22) - the class could not reach zero while these sat in it. Seven tests in tests/test_fixture_epoch_exclusion.py, two asserting against the live config.

SCHEMA GAP, found by CQ-27: no edge type in kg/schema.yaml links a Framework to an Instrument, so no competency question can ever ask which framework owns which instrument. MEASURED: 506 Framework nodes and 502 Instrument nodes are in the graph and there are ZERO relationships of ANY type between them (MATCH (f:Framework)-[r]-(i:Instrument) returns no rows). It is not an extraction gap. The schema's edge types touching these labels are operationalizes (Instrument->Construct), measures (Measure|Instrument -> Construct|Concept), uses_measure (Instrument->Measure), has_component (Framework|Concept -> Concept), extends (Definition|Framework -> Definition|Framework) and builds_on (Standard|Framework -> Standard|Framework). None has domain Framework and range Instrument, so the parser's edge whitelist would reject such an edge even if the model asserted it. CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this is filed high: CQ-27 was written to test the re-scoped G1 claim from Issue cfe9eaf7 -- that no AI-READINESS ASSESSMENT instrument measures uncertainty legibility -- and its pre-registered criterion says an empty answer counts as evidence only if both legs are live. Leg 1 is live (11 Instrument-MEASURES-Concept rows on uncertainty terms). Leg 2 is dead by construction. CQ-27 therefore scores 'no': the question was not testable and nothing was learned about the claim. The claim stays untested until the schema admits a framework-to-instrument relationship, which per invariant 4 goes through the schema doc's §6 review and never a silent edit. Registered by task cc_tasks/2026-09-05_vocabulary_and_entity_linking.md §4.

properties.terminal_reason: Reframed as vocabulary-first; see cc_tasks/2026-09-05_vocabulary_and_entity_linking.md. This task specified a one-time dedup pass producing canonical nodes with SAME_AS edges. The replacement makes the fix a CONTROLLED VOCABULARY that every mention resolves against at WRITE time (loader-side, build_projection.py §1.4), evolved by epochs, rather than a batch job over a snapshot — because the evidence says a one-time pass would not have held: the 2026-09-05 strand extraction added 795 Concepts and moved flip by exactly zero, so the statistic tracks graph structure and not corpus size, and a dedup run once over a 'complete' corpus would be stale the next time anything is extracted. The design layers are the same ones this task named (deterministic pre-dedup, LLM-proposed merges with confidence, reviewable YAML) and the prior art is now cited: Cutter 1876 / ISO 25964 / W3C SKOS for the vocabulary, Fellegi-Sunter 1969 for the three-way threshold split, Franklin-Halevy-Maier 2005 and Madhavan 2007 for pay-as-you-go promotion. Delivered: 1,946 terms at epoch 1, RESOLVES_TO on 6,408 nodes, Cohen's kappa 0.979 against an independent rater, and a third  view in the CQ harness. Its acceptance criterion FAILED and is reported as a result.
